By the 1950s and 60s Norway had its own modern school: Jakob Weidemann turned the Norwegian forest floor into abstraction, and Gunnar S. Gundersen built pictures from flat, hard-edged fields of colour that look like they could have been made yesterday. The through-line from them to now is the thing to notice: Nordic modernism rarely abandoned the subject. It pared the subject back, a forest floor, a bird, a table, until the shape could carry it alone.
